expo.name: pew2
expo.//scheme: Claims the `pew2://` URL scheme. The one link routed is `pew2://open?session=<id>`, from the home/Lock Screen widget, and all it can do is open a conversation already in the list (`conversationFromLink` in src/widgetSnapshot.ts) — it cannot pair, prompt or approve, so any app being able to open it costs nothing. Pairing stays camera-only on purpose: a link that paired on arrival would let any app point this phone at someone else's daemon, so that handler needs a confirmation step designed before it exists.
expo.//runtimeVersion: Which native binary an over-the-air update may load. `appVersion` ties it to the version above, so an update built against changed native code can never be handed to a build that cannot run it — the failure being a launch loop on a phone with no way back. Actually publishing updates needs `updates.url` from `eas init`, which requires an account this repository does not carry; until then this ships the client without a source.
expo.//orientation: Unlocked, so the app follows the device. Half of what an agent replies with is wide — a table, a diff, a fenced command line — and on a 390-point screen those wrap into a column of fragments; turning the phone is the one thing the reader can do about that which costs nothing. The layout follows rather than assuming: the drawer's width and the sheets' row counts are read per render (useDrawerWidth, useSheetVisibleRows) instead of sampled once at import, and the conversation pane takes left/right safe-area insets, because a notch on a long edge does not fade content out like the CanvasCovers do at top and bottom — it hides it.

ios.//supportsTablet: False for 1.0 because nothing here is built for a tablet: the layout is portrait-only phone chrome, no code branches on an iPad idiom, and no iPad screenshots exist — App Store Connect requires a 13-inch set the moment this is true, and review then tests the stretched phone UI on hardware it was never laid out for. Turning it on is a layout pass plus its own screenshot set, not a flag.
ios.//: Reverse-DNS of the GitHub org that hosts this, not a domain: `pew2.dev` is not registered, and an identifier built from a domain someone else can buy is a claim that can be contested after the app is on a store — at which point it cannot be changed without shipping a new app. Fork this and you must change it: an identifier is unique per store, and a fork keeping this one cannot be submitted alongside the original.
ios.//appleTeamId: The team every target is signed by. Required by @bacons/apple-targets so the widget and notification extensions are signed like the app; public (it is in every signed binary), not a secret.
ios.//entitlements: The App Group the home/Lock Screen widget reads from: the app writes `pew2.snapshot` there (src/ui/useHomeWidget.ts), and so does the notification service extension when a push lands while the app is asleep (targets/notifications). Both targets mirror this value from here.
ios.//infoPlist: Ships verbatim into Info.plist, so no comment keys inside it — Apple reads what is written there. `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: false` answers the export-compliance question at build time instead of halting every upload to ask it. The answer is honest: this app's own cryptography is the pairing seal in @pew2/protocol (XChaCha20-Poly1305 and HKDF-SHA256 from @noble) over TLS, both exempt under the standard 'uses only encryption exempt from EAR' category. Adding a non-exempt algorithm of our own means revisiting this line, not merely the answer in the console. `UIBackgroundModes: [audio]` keeps a live voice conversation running with the screen locked or the phone in a pocket; expo-notifications merges its own `remote-notification` into the same array at prebuild.

infoPlist.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Used to connect to the pew2 daemon running on your computer when both are on the same network.

android.//blockedPermissions: The WebRTC config plugin adds SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW for screen-sharing overlays, which this app never draws and which Play review asks to justify.

plugins.//: Without this the generated splash is pure white while the app's own background is theme.color.bg with userInterfaceStyle dark, so every cold launch flashed white before painting. No `dark` variant: the app is dark-only, and declaring one conflicts with the app-wide userInterfaceStyle. The colour is theme.color.bg, kept in step by hand because app.json cannot import it. The image is Pew from scripts/make-icon.py, lifted off that same colour so its glow composes back exactly; 250 makes his globe the size LaunchScreen's Pew opens at, so the handoff does not jump.

false removes NSFaceIDUsageDescription. Nothing here stores with requireAuthentication, and the plugin otherwise ships its generic Face ID string, a purpose string for a permission the app never asks for.

One string for two uses: scanning the pairing code, and taking a photo to send an agent. expo-image-picker writes the same Info.plist key, so its own cameraPermission is deliberately left unset rather than fighting this one.
plugins.cameraPermission: Used to scan the pairing code shown on your computer, and to take photos you send to your agent.

plugins.//: For the connecting ringtone only: it records nothing, so it must not touch NSMicrophoneUsageDescription (expo-speech-recognition owns that key) and must not ask for background recording.

No photosPermission here on purpose: expo-media-library below writes the same NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription key and runs later, so a string here would be overwritten and the attach prompt would explain saving instead of attaching. That one string covers both uses.

plugins.microphonePermission: Used to dictate a message while the mic button is on, and to talk with your voice assistant during a live voice conversation you start.
plugins.speechRecognitionPermission: Used only to turn what you dictate into the text of a message.
plugins.//: The one owner of NSMicrophoneUsageDescription. The WebRTC plugin below is given no microphonePermission and only fills the key when it is empty, so this string covers dictation and live voice.
No microphonePermission or cameraPermission: expo-speech-recognition and expo-camera own those keys, and this plugin keeps an existing value.

plugins.savePhotosPermission: Used only to save images your agent sends you.
plugins.photosPermission: Used only to attach photos you pick, and to save images your agent sends you.

expo.//experiments: The React Compiler memoises components automatically — the same work as the hand-written memo/useCallback in Sidebar and ChatThread, which is what stopped the drawer recomputing its lists on the frame it starts moving. Those stay: they document intent, and the compiler is a floor under them rather than a replacement. Which files it may touch is decided by `sources` in babel.config.js, not here — this flag is only the on switch, and turning it on without that filter would hand it the daemon hook too, where a dropped update reads as a reply that never arrived rather than as a slow screen.
